issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a fully implemented class named Meal (with constructor and getters). However, the template repository does not provide a Meal implementation (Meal.java is empty) and instead includes an Order.java class with the same shape as the expected Meal. The solution repository implements Meal. This name/type mismatch (Order vs Meal) and the missing Meal in the template will confuse students and block them from following the specification and tests that refer to Meal.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a Meal class in the template matching the problem statement (constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters). Remove or rename the extraneous Order.java (or clearly document why Order exists). Ensure Main and other template references use Meal so students implement and test against the expected class name and API.

issues.description: The problem statement and reference solution consistently refer to the core entity as class 'Meal' (with fields name and ingredients), but the template repository provides an implemented 'Order' class and an empty Meal.java. This mismatch (Meal vs Order) refers to the same conceptual entity (a meal/order item) with different identifiers across artifacts and will confuse students when mapping requirements to the starter code and expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Either (A) rename the template's 'Order' class to 'Meal' (and update any references in the template Main and other files) so the starter matches the problem description and solution, or (B) update the problem statement to use 'Order' consistently. Recommended: replace Order.java with a Meal.java implementing the same fields/constructor used in the problem statement to avoid student confusion.
